app.name: PoC Automation 3.0
app.description: All in One, automated Dynatrace PoC: coverage, evidence, value and Tech Wrapup

scopes.name: storage:entities:read
scopes.comment: Inventory of hosts, services, applications, processes, Kubernetes and synthetic monitors (entity model reads, 0 bytes scanned).

scopes.name: storage:smartscape:read
scopes.comment: Smartscape on Grail (smartscapeNodes): cloud service families and Kubernetes pods. Required by the platform for smartscapeNodes/smartscapeEdges; without it those two queries are refused.

scopes.name: storage:events:read
scopes.comment: Problems (dt.davis.problems), Kubernetes operational events and synthetic events.

scopes.name: storage:system:read
scopes.comment: dt.system.events: billing usage, workflow and query execution events, platform adoption and the billing of the app's own queries.

scopes.name: storage:buckets:read
scopes.comment: dt.system.buckets: retention, volume and has_access for the coverage matrix.

scopes.name: storage:logs:read
scopes.comment: Log volume, levels and data-quality signals. Always bucket-scoped and scan-limited.

scopes.name: storage:metrics:read
scopes.comment: Timeseries for host, service, Kubernetes and real-user trends, SLO indicators and the GenAI metrics of AI Observability.

scopes.name: storage:bizevents:read
scopes.comment: Business observability. Validated: 1,099,009 records / 24h.

scopes.name: storage:security.events:read
scopes.comment: Vulnerabilities and runtime risk. Without it the app shows an explicit no-permission state.

scopes.name: storage:user.sessions:read
scopes.comment: Real user monitoring sessions. Without access the app shows an explicit gap state.

scopes.name: state:app-states:read
scopes.comment: Reads the PoC configuration saved on the tenant (customer, scope, logos, pillars, partner access). Shared by every user of the app.

scopes.name: state:app-states:write
scopes.comment: Saves the PoC configuration on the tenant so it is still there when the app is reopened.

scopes.name: state:app-states:delete
scopes.comment: "New PoC": deletes the saved configuration.

scopes.name: state:user-app-states:read
scopes.comment: Reads the user's own working figures (rates, price-table setting, baseline, language). Readable only by that user.

scopes.name: state:user-app-states:write
scopes.comment: Saves the user's own working figures.

scopes.name: state:user-app-states:delete
scopes.comment: "New PoC": deletes the user's own saved figures.

scopes.name: document:documents:write
scopes.comment: Since 3.2.5: creates and updates the dashboards, the investigation notebook and the launchpad of the PoC Builder, only when the SE clicks and confirms; never at deploy or on its own. Since 3.2.7 the real-prints tab (SE Report) also keeps two private documents of the SE's own: the print set (JSON) and a ZIP of the SE's screenshots; "New PoC" overwrites both with an empty tombstone. Since 3.7.7 the weekly workflow action writes the week's report notebook with the workflow actor's permissions.

scopes.name: document:documents:delete
scopes.comment: Since 3.6.9: the PoC Builder's end-of-PoC clean-up removes the dashboards, the notebook and the launchpad this PoC created — only the documents in the PoC's register, only after the SE ticks them and confirms; never on its own.

scopes.name: slo:slos:read
scopes.comment: Since 3.6.9: reads the current version of an SLO this PoC created, which the platform needs before removing it (optimistic lock).

scopes.name: slo:slos:write
scopes.comment: Since 3.6.9: creates the availability, performance and fleet SLOs the SE picks on the PoC Builder (indicators from the query catalog) and removes them in the end-of-PoC clean-up — only on the SE's click.

scopes.name: document:documents:read
scopes.comment: Since 3.2.5: reads the version of a document this app created, so updating it replaces the same document instead of creating a copy; reads back the SE's own private print set and screenshot ZIP of the real-prints tab.

scopes.name: environment-api:synthetic:read
scopes.comment: Since 3.7.3: lists the environment's public synthetic locations, so the SE picks where the PoC's HTTP and Browser monitors run.

scopes.name: environment-api:synthetic-monitors:write
scopes.comment: Since 3.7.3: creates the HTTP and Browser monitors of the customer's addresses the SE confirms on the PoC Builder, and removes them in the end-of-PoC clean-up — only on the SE's click.

scopes.name: settings:objects:write
scopes.comment: Since 3.7.4: creates the Davis anomaly detectors of the golden signals (builtin:davis.anomaly-detectors; since 3.8.0 run by a service user — since 3.8.1 the one set in Settings) and the OpenPipeline logs pipeline that gives a level to logs written without one (builtin:openpipeline.logs.pipelines), and writes back the logs routing with the PoC's route — only on the SE's click — and removes them in the end-of-PoC clean-up.

scopes.name: settings:objects:read
scopes.comment: Since 3.7.6: reads the OpenPipeline logs routing (builtin:openpipeline.logs.routing) — one settings object whose list of routes other pipelines share — so the PoC Builder adds the PoC pipeline's route at the top, and the clean-up removes it, without touching the other routes.

scopes.name: iam:service-users:use
scopes.comment: Since 3.8.2: lets the PoC Builder write the anomaly detectors with the service user the SE set in Settings as their actor (executionSettings.actor) — without it the settings service answers 'User has no permission to use service users'.

img-src.comment: Real-prints tab: the print thumbnails, the print editor and the crop dialog show the SE's own screenshots from in-memory Blobs (object URLs); nothing is loaded from another origin.

actions.name: poc-triage
actions.title: PoC Automation · Triage
actions.description: Reads a problem, its logs around the incident and the callers of its root cause, and returns a summary to send.

actions.name: poc-weekly
actions.title: PoC Automation · Weekly
actions.description: Reads the last seven days of problems against the week before and returns a weekly PoC summary to send.
